title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Wall Street enters Black Friday's shortened session (1pm ET close) looking to extend gains after Wednesday's close, when the Dow reclaimed the 50,000 mark while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq stayed softer on lingering AI-stock weakness.
Markets: November has been a volatile month for tech, with the Nasdaq on track to snap a multi-month win streak as investors reassess AI-related valuations.
Companies: Nvidia shares remain under pressure this week amid S&P's credit-watch warning and growing worries that hyperscalers' in-house AI chips threaten its margins.
Companies: Alphabet had one of its worst weeks since 2008 even as its custom TPU chips are seen as a competitive threat to Nvidia; Amazon also traded lower on AI-capex jitters.
Macro/Policy: The Fed held rates steady at its October 28 meeting; traders remain split on whether a December 9 cut is still likely as year-end rate-cut odds turn more uncertain.
Macro/Policy: No major US economic data is due in the holiday-shortened week; markets continue digesting the administration's proposed tariffs on China, Vietnam, the EU and other trading partners.
